dc21.title: Activity feed: Load more
dc21.summary: A deploy dashboard needs its activity feed: load page 1 on mount, then append pages with a Load more button until there are none left.
dc21.brief:
Shipyard is a deploy dashboard. App.tsx has Sidebar, StatCard and an empty ActivityFeed card. Your job is the feed.

Read api.ts first: getActivity(page) returns { items, nextPage }, where nextPage is null on the last page. It takes a random 0.5–1.2 s. There are 13 events, 5 per page.

Worth reading too: components/ActivityItem.tsx already renders one row (icon, text, time via utils/time.ts). Reuse it; don't rebuild the row.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next.

Timeline: 0–2 read · 2–4 plan · 4–12 Core · 12–15 Next + check

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"All the state lives in ActivityFeed: items, nextPage and loading. The API tells me the next page, so I store nextPage instead of counting pages myself. On mount I fetch page 1 with a cancelled guard. Load more fetches nextPage and appends with setItems((prev) => [...prev, ...page.items]). The button only renders while nextPage !== null, says Loading… and is disabled while a request is in flight, which also stops double clicks from fetching the same page twice."
requirements: On mount the card shows "Loading activity…", then the first 5 events, each rendered with the existing <ActivityItem />
A Load more button under the list fetches the next page and appends it (the first 5 stay; now 10 rows). While it loads, the button reads Loading… and is disabled
After the last page (13 rows) the button disappears
In its place a muted line reads "You're all caught up · 13 events". Rapid double clicks never load the same page twice
hints: Three pieces of state: the list, the next page number (or null), and a loading flag. Where does each one come from?
Mount fetch: useEffect(() => { let cancelled = false; getActivity(1).then((page) => { if (cancelled) { return; } ... }); return () => { cancelled = true; }; }, []);
Appending must use the updater form, because the old list is what you add to: setItems((prev) => { return [...prev, ...page.items]; });
Search: "react disable button while loading". Disabled buttons don't fire onClick, which is your double-click guard. Add an early if (loading || nextPage === null) { return; } too.
Shape: let footer = null; if (items.length > 0 && nextPage !== null) { footer = <button ...>{label}</button>; } else if (items.length > 0) { footer = <p>You're all caught up</p>; }
rubric: Stored nextPage from the API instead of computing pages by hand
Mount fetch has a cancelled guard and cleanup
Appends with the updater form; never mutates or replaces the list
Reused ActivityItem instead of rebuilding the row
Button label/disabled derived from loading; no duplicate requests
End state handled (button removed, caught-up line)

dc22.title: Blog editor: tag input
dc22.summary: Turn the plain Tags field of a blog editor into a chip input: Enter or comma adds, Backspace removes, no duplicates, max 5.
dc22.brief:
Inkwell is a blogging editor. App.tsx has TopBar, Editor, PostSettings and a TagField that is just a text input for now.

Read utils/tags.ts (cleanTag and MAX_TAGS) and components/Chip.tsx (a chip that shows a × when you pass onRemove). Both are meant to be reused. No API in this one.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next.

Timeline: 0–2 read · 2–4 plan · 4–14 Core · 14–18 Next

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The tags belong to the post, so tags goes in App and comes down to TagField with an onChange. The half-typed text and the error message are local to TagField. Everything happens in one onKeyDown: Enter or comma calls addTag (with preventDefault so the comma isn't typed), and Backspace on an empty draft drops the last tag. addTag cleans the text, then checks max, then duplicates with some on lowercase."
requirements: Typing a tag and pressing Enter or , adds it as a <Chip> inside the box, before the input, and clears the input. The comma is never typed. Text is cleaned with cleanTag; empty tags are ignored
Each chip's × removes it. Backspace in an empty input removes the last chip
Duplicates are ignored case-insensitively ("React" then "react" adds one chip) and show "react" is already added.
At 5 tags, adding another shows You can add up to 5 tags. and does not add it. Normally the help line reads "Press Enter or comma to add · 2 / 5"
tags lives in App (the post owns it); TagField only owns the draft and the message
hints: Which component needs the tags when you click Publish later? That's where tags lives.
Search: "mdn keydown event key". e.key is "Enter", "," or "Backspace".
Search: "react onKeyDown preventDefault". Without e.preventDefault() the comma lands in the input.
Duplicate check: tags.some((t) => { return t.toLowerCase() === tag.toLowerCase(); })

Shape: function handleKeyDown(e: React.KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) { if (e.key === "Enter" || e.key === ",") { e.preventDefault(); addTag(); return; } if (e.key === "Backspace" && draft === "" && tags.length > 0) { onChange(tags.slice(0, -1)); } }
rubric: Put tags in the owner (App) and passed an onChange down
One onKeyDown handler; preventDefault for Enter/comma
Reused cleanTag, MAX_TAGS and Chip
Case-insensitive duplicate check with some()
New arrays only (spread, filter, slice); no push/splice on state
Message state cleared on success; help line derived

dc23.title: Pomodoro timer
dc23.summary: Make a focus timer actually tick: Start/Pause, Reset, mm:ss, and an automatic 5-minute break at 00:00, with exactly one interval.
dc23.brief:
Ripe is a focus app. App.tsx has Header, Timer (static 25:00 with Start/Reset buttons that do nothing), SessionDots and a TaskList from components/.

Read utils/time.ts: formatTime(seconds) gives "mm:ss", and FOCUS_SECONDS / BREAK_SECONDS are already defined. No API in this one.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next.

Timeline: 0–2 read · 2–4 plan · 4–14 Core · 14–18 Next

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"I store secondsLeft, running and mode in Timer. The display is formatTime(secondsLeft), never a stored string. One effect depends on running: if running, it starts setInterval and the cleanup clears it, so pausing, resetting or unmounting always kills it and there's never a second one. The tick uses setSecondsLeft((s) => s - 1) because the interval closure would see a stale value. A second effect watches for 0 and switches mode. The finished-session count goes up to App through an onFocusComplete callback, because SessionDots needs it."
requirements: Start counts down once per second from 25:00 in mm:ss (24:59, 24:58…). While running the button reads Pause; Pause stops it, Start resumes from the same time
Exactly one interval ever runs: clicking Start/Pause quickly many times never makes it tick faster, and the interval is cleared on pause, reset and unmount
At 00:00 the timer switches to Break (pill reads "Break", green style) at 05:00 and keeps running. When the break hits 00:00 it returns to Focus 25:00 and stops
Reset stops the timer and returns to Focus 25:00. Each completed focus session fills one dot: "1 of 4 sessions"
A thin progress bar under the time fills as the current session runs (derived from secondsLeft)
hints: What has to be state? Seconds left, running or not, focus or break. The "mm:ss" text is derived.
Search: "react setInterval useEffect cleanup". The effect depends on [running]; return () => { clearInterval(id); }.
Inside setInterval, secondsLeft is frozen at the value from when the effect ran. Use setSecondsLeft((s) => { return s - 1; });
Switching at zero: a second effect on [secondsLeft, mode]: if (secondsLeft > 0) { return; } if (mode === "focus") { setMode("break"); setSecondsLeft(BREAK_SECONDS); onFocusComplete(); } else { ... }
Shape: useEffect(() => { if (!running) { return; } const id = setInterval(() => { setSecondsLeft((s) => { return s - 1; }); }, 1000); return () => { clearInterval(id); }; }, [running]);
rubric: Interval lives in an effect keyed on running, with clearInterval cleanup
Tick uses the updater form (no stale closure)
Display derived with the existing formatTime helper
Mode switch at zero handled once, cleanly
Session count lifted to App through a callback
Explained why double intervals can't happen

notes: pill, border, button and bar turn leaf green

dc24.title: Dashboard theme switcher
dc24.summary: Add Light / Dark / System to an analytics dashboard with CSS variables on a data-theme attribute, remembered in localStorage.
dc24.brief:
Northwind Metrics is a SaaS dashboard: KPI cards, a revenue chart and an invoice table. Every color in styles.css comes from variables on :root.

Read components/SegmentedControl.tsx: the date-range switch already uses it, and the theme switch should too. No API in this one.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next.

Timeline: 0–2 read · 2–4 plan · 4–13 Core · 13–18 Next

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"I store the user's choice (light, dark or system) in App, initialised lazily from localStorage inside a try/catch, because storage can throw. The applied theme is derived: the choice, or the OS theme when the choice is system. I put it on the root div as data-theme, and in CSS .app[data-theme="dark"] redefines the variables, which inherit to everything inside. Saving happens in the click handler. For live OS changes I listen to matchMedia change in an effect with cleanup."
requirements: A second SegmentedControl labelled "Theme" in the top bar with Light, Dark, System. The app root gets data-theme="light" or "dark"
Dark mode is done only in CSS: .app[data-theme="dark"] redefines the color variables (bg #0B1120, surface #131B2E, text #E2E8F0…). No component changes its own colors
The choice is saved to localStorage key northwind-theme and restored on reload. Every storage read and write is wrapped in try/catch; with no saved value the default is System
System follows prefers-color-scheme, live: changing the OS setting updates the page without a reload. Next to the switch a muted note reads "Using dark" / "Using light" while System is chosen
hints: Two different things: what the user picked (3 options) and what's applied (2 options). Only the first one is state.
Search: "css custom properties override attribute selector". Variables inherit, so redefining them on .app beats the :root values for everything inside.
Search: "mdn localStorage exceptions". getItem and setItem can throw (private mode, blocked storage). Wrap both.
Lazy initial state reads storage once: useState<ThemeChoice>(() => { return readStoredChoice(); })

Search: "mdn matchMedia change event". Shape: const mq = window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"); mq.addEventListener("change", handle); return () => { mq.removeEventListener("change", handle); };
rubric: Stored the choice; derived the applied theme
Dark theme done purely by redefining variables under data-theme
localStorage wrapped in try/catch, read lazily once
Reused SegmentedControl
matchMedia listener added and removed in an effect
Validated the stored value instead of trusting it

notes: same SegmentedControl · after date range · gap 10

dc25.title: Chat composer: emoji picker
dc25.summary: A team-chat composer gets an emoji popover: categories from an API, insert at the cursor, close on outside click or Escape.
dc25.brief:
Huddle is a team chat. App.tsx has Sidebar, the message list (using components/Message.tsx) and a working Composer: type, Send appends a message. The 🙂 button in the composer bar does nothing yet.

Read api.ts: getEmojiCategories() returns 3 categories (name, tab icon, emojis) after a random 0.4–1.0 s.

The hard part is inserting where the cursor is, not at the end. The textarea keeps its selection after it loses focus.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~18 min): a recently used row.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan · 5–18 Core · 18–24 change · 24–28 Next + talk

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"text lives in Composer, so pickerOpen and handlePick go there too. I make an EmojiPicker that's only mounted while open and loads the categories itself, with a tab per category. For the cursor I need a ref on the textarea: read selectionStart/selectionEnd, splice the emoji into the text, then after the re-render put the caret after the emoji. The button and the popover share a wrapper ref; a mousedown listener on document closes it when the click is outside that wrapper, and a keydown listener handles Escape. Both are added only while open and removed in the cleanup."
requirements: Clicking 🙂 toggles a popover above the button. It shows "Loading emoji…" until getEmojiCategories() resolves, then one tab per category (its icon) and an 8-column grid of that category's emojis under its name
Clicking an emoji inserts it at the cursor (replacing any selected text), not at the end: with "See you" and the caret after "See", picking 😀 gives "See😀 you". Then the popover closes
The popover closes on a click outside it and on Escape. Clicking inside it (e.g. switching tabs) keeps it open
After inserting, the textarea is focused with the caret right after the emoji, so typing continues there
Listeners are only attached while open and are removed on close (effect cleanup)

change.title: Recently used row
change.html:
"People use the same five emoji all day. Put them at the top."

  • When at least one emoji has been picked, the popover shows a Recently used row above the tabs.
  • Most recent first, no duplicates (picking one again moves it to the front), at most 8.
  • It must survive the popover closing and reopening.

Hint: the picker unmounts on close, so this state can't live in it.

hints: Where does the text live? The picker only reports which emoji; the composer changes the text.
Search: "mdn HTMLTextAreaElement selectionStart". el.selectionStart and el.selectionEnd are indexes into the value.
Insert: text.slice(0, start) + emoji + text.slice(end). Emoji are usually 2 UTF-16 units, so the new caret is start + emoji.length.
Search: "mdn setSelectionRange". The caret must be set after React re-renders: keep it in a ref and apply it in a useEffect on [text].
Outside click: put the button and popover in one wrapper with a ref, then if (wrapRef.current && !wrapRef.current.contains(e.target as Node)) { setPickerOpen(false); } in a mousedown listener.
Recent: setRecent((prev) => { return [emoji, ...prev.filter((x) => { return x !== emoji; })].slice(0, 8); }); in Composer.
rubric: Planned state placement (text, open, recent in Composer)
Used selectionStart/selectionEnd and restored the caret after render
Picker loads its own data with a loading state and cancelled guard
Outside click uses one wrapper ref so the toggle button doesn't reopen it
Document listeners added only while open and cleaned up
Recent row is deduped, capped, most-recent-first, and survives close
Talked through anything unfinished

notes: w 296 · pad 10 · radius 12 · bottom 40 above button

dc26.title: People search: debounce + races
dc26.summary: A company directory search: 300 ms debounce, loading state, and stale responses that must never overwrite newer ones.
dc26.brief:
Roster is an HR directory. App.tsx has the top bar, a SearchBox (controlled) and a PersonRow that uses components/Avatar.tsx. Typing does nothing yet.

Read api.ts carefully: searchPeople(query) is slower for shorter queries ("j" ≈ 1.3 s, "jan" ≈ 0.7 s). So if you search "j" and then "jan", the "j" answer arrives last. A naive version shows the wrong results.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~17 min): highlight the match.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan · 5–17 Core · 17–22 change · 22–25 Next + talk

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"query is state; results and loading are state because they come from the network. One effect on [query] does everything: if the query is empty it clears results and returns. Otherwise it starts a 300 ms setTimeout that calls the API. The cleanup does two jobs: clearTimeout (that's the debounce, because every keystroke cancels the pending call) and cancelled = true (so a response from an older query is ignored when it arrives late)."
requirements: Typing searches with searchPeople, debounced 300 ms: typing "jan" quickly makes one request, not three
While a request is in flight a "Searching…" line shows under the search box; results render with <PersonRow />. No matches: No people match "xyz".
Out-of-order responses never win: type "j", wait ~0.4 s, then type "an". After everything settles the list shows the 5 "jan" people, not the 7 "j" people
Empty input (or clearing it) shows "Start typing to search 18 people." with no request and no Searching… line
Old results stay visible (dimmed) while a newer search loads, instead of flashing empty

change.title: Highlight the match
change.html:
"People scan the list for why it matched. Highlight it."

  • In each name, wrap the first case-insensitive match of the query in <mark> (teal-soft background, dark teal text). "jan" in "Ben Janssen" highlights "Jan".
  • Highlight with the query the results belong to, not the one being typed right now.

Hint: no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Split the string into before / match / after.

hints: Debounce in React is just setTimeout in an effect plus clearTimeout in the cleanup.
Search: "react useEffect race condition fetch". The fix is a let cancelled = false per effect run, set to true in the cleanup.
The cleanup runs before the next effect run, so when query changes, the previous run is cancelled both ways: its timer and its response.
Highlight: const i = text.toLowerCase().indexOf(q.toLowerCase()); then text.slice(0, i), text.slice(i, i + q.length), text.slice(i + q.length).

Shape: useEffect(() => { if (q === "") { ...; return; } let cancelled = false; const t = setTimeout(() => { setLoading(true); searchPeople(q).then((data) => { if (cancelled) { return; } setResults(data); setLoading(false); }); }, 300); return () => { cancelled = true; clearTimeout(t); }; }, [query]);
rubric: Explained the race before coding it
Debounce via setTimeout + clearTimeout in cleanup
Stale responses ignored via cancelled flag
Empty query short-circuits (no request)
Loading and empty states are distinct and correct
Highlight derived by slicing, uses the results' query
Reused Avatar / PersonRow

dc27.title: Kanban: move cards
dc27.summary: Load a roadmap board from an API, move cards between To do / Doing / Done with arrows, count each column, add cards. Then a WIP limit.
dc27.brief:
Trellis is a project board. App.tsx has CardView, Column and an empty Board. The columns render, but there are no cards yet.

Read api.ts (getCards(), random 0.5–1.2 s; each card has a column) and board.ts (COLUMNS in left-to-right order, and label names).

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~19 min): WIP limit on Doing.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan · 5–19 Core · 19–24 change · 24–28 Next + talk

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"One flat cards array in Board, where each card knows its column. The columns are derived with filter, so I never keep three lists in sync. Moving is map: same card with column set to the next or previous entry in COLUMNS. The counts are just .length of the filtered lists. The add form is its own small component with its own input state that calls onAdd(title)."
requirements: The board shows "Loading board…", then the cards from getCards() in their columns. Each column header shows a count pill: To do 3, Doing 2, Done 2
Each card has ← and → buttons that move it to the previous / next column. ← is disabled in To do and → in Done. Counts update
Under To do, an input + Add button (a form, so Enter works) adds a card with that title to the bottom of To do and clears the input. Blank titles are ignored
Cards are updated immutably by id (map + spread); the columns are derived from one array, never three separate lists

change.title: WIP limit on Doing
change.html:
"The team keeps starting things and never finishing. Limit Doing to 3."

  • Doing's count reads 2 / 3, and turns red at 3 / 3.
  • Moving a card into Doing when it has 3 is blocked: the card stays, and a red banner above the board says Doing is at its WIP limit of 3. Finish something first.
  • Any successful move clears the banner.

hints: One array or three? If each card stores its column, a move is a one-field change.
Next column: const from = COLUMNS.findIndex((c) => { return c.id === card.column; }); const target = COLUMNS[from + step]; where step is -1 or 1.
Move: setCards((prev) => { return prev.map((c) => { if (c.id !== id) { return c; } return { ...c, column: target.id }; }); });
Search: "react form onSubmit preventDefault" for the add form, so Enter submits without reloading.
WIP: check before moving: if (target.id === "doing" && cardsIn("doing").length >= WIP_LIMIT) { setNotice(...); return; }
rubric: Single source of truth (flat array) with derived columns
Fetch on mount with loading state and cancelled guard
Immutable move by id; edges disabled
Add form is controlled, uses onSubmit + preventDefault, ignores blanks
WIP rule checked before the update, with clear feedback
Column component stays presentational (props + callbacks)

dc28.title: Comments: inline replies
dc28.summary: On a recipe page, Reply opens one inline box under that comment; posting is async with a pending state. Then collapsible replies.
dc28.brief:
Simmer is a recipe site. App.tsx loads the comments (already done) and renders CommentItem with its ReplyItems. Each comment has a Reply link that does nothing yet.

Read api.ts: postReply(commentId, text) resolves after a random 0.7–1.2 s with the new Reply. components/Avatar.tsx and utils/time.ts are worth reusing.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~19 min): collapsible replies.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan · 5–19 Core · 19–25 change · 25–28 Next + talk

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Only one reply box can be open, so CommentSection stores replyingTo: string | null, the id of the comment, not a boolean per comment. A ReplyBox component owns its draft and its pending flag. On submit it calls onSubmit(text), which returns the promise from postReply. When it resolves, the section adds the reply into that comment's replies with a nested map + spread and sets replyingTo to null, which unmounts the box."
requirements: Clicking Reply opens an inline reply box (textarea + Cancel + Post reply) under that comment only. Clicking Reply on another comment moves the box there. Cancel closes it
Post reply calls postReply. While pending the button reads Posting… and the textarea and buttons are disabled. Blank text can't be posted
When it resolves, the reply appears at the end of that comment's replies (author "You", "just now") and the box closes. State is updated immutably
The textarea is focused when the box opens and its placeholder reads "Reply to Nadia Q.…"

change.title: Collapse / expand replies
change.html:
"Long threads push the next comments off screen."

  • Replies start collapsed. Under a comment with replies, a muted link reads Show 3 replies (or Show 1 reply). Clicking shows them and the link becomes Hide replies.
  • Comments without replies show no link.
  • After you post a reply, that thread is expanded so you can see it.

hints: How many reply boxes can be open at once? One. So store which comment, not a flag per comment.
Search: "react async form submit loading state". Set pending to true before the call; the box unmounts on success, so you don't need to set it back.
Nested update: prev.map((c) => { if (c.id !== commentId) { return c; } return { ...c, replies: [...c.replies, reply] }; })
Return the promise: function handlePostReply(id, text) { return postReply(id, text).then((reply) => { ... }); }
Collapse: const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState<Record<string, boolean>>({}); and toggle with setExpanded((prev) => { return { ...prev, [id]: !prev[id] }; });
rubric: replyingTo stores one id; only one box possible
Pending state disables input and changes the label
Nested immutable update (map + spread twice)
ReplyBox owns draft; section owns data
Collapse state keyed by id, label pluralised, expands after posting
Reused Avatar and timeAgo

dc29.title: Travel listing: photo carousel
dc29.summary: A vacation rental page shows one photo. Make it a carousel: wrapping prev/next, dots, a counter, and autoplay that pauses on hover.
dc29.brief:
Wanderstay is a vacation rental site. App.tsx loads the listing (already done) and renders Gallery, which only shows the first photo, plus details and a BookingCard.

Read components/PhotoSlide.tsx: it renders any photo. Reuse it for the current slide. There are 7 photos.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~18 min): keyboard arrows.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan · 5–18 Core · 18–22 change · 22–25 Next + talk

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Gallery owns index and paused. Next is (i + 1) % count, prev is (i - 1 + count) % count so it wraps both ways. Autoplay is an effect with setInterval that skips when paused and clears in the cleanup. I'll put index in its deps so a manual click restarts the 4 s countdown. Hover sets paused with onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave. The counter is derived: index + 1 of count."
requirements: Round ‹ / › buttons on the photo go to the previous / next photo, wrapping (next on 7 goes to 1, prev on 1 goes to 7)
A row of dots at the bottom (active one white and larger); clicking a dot jumps to that photo. A pill at the bottom right reads 3 / 7
Autoplay advances every 4 s. It pauses while the mouse is over the carousel and resumes on leave. The interval is cleared on unmount and never doubles up
A manual move restarts the 4 s countdown (no jump right after a click)

change.title: Keyboard arrows
change.html:
"Accessibility review: the carousel can't be used without a mouse."

  • The carousel is focusable (tabIndex={0}, visible focus ring) with role="region" and aria-label="Listing photos".
  • While it has focus, ArrowLeft / ArrowRight go prev / next (same wrapping).
  • Arrow keys elsewhere on the page do nothing to it.

hints: Wrapping is modulo. Going back: add count before % so it never goes negative.
Search: "react setInterval useEffect cleanup". Return early when paused; the cleanup clears the interval.
Inside the interval use the updater: setIndex((i) => { return (i + 1) % count; });
Search: "mdn mouseenter vs mouseover". onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave don't fire again for children.
Search: "mdn tabindex" and "react onKeyDown". Put onKeyDown on the focusable carousel div, not on document.
rubric: Index-only state; counter and active dot derived
Correct wrap both directions
Interval in an effect with cleanup; pause state respected
Reused PhotoSlide
Keyboard handled on the focusable element, not globally
ARIA labels on icon buttons and dots

notes: 36 circle · 14 from edge · vertically centered · shadow

dc30.title: Coffee shop: cart drawer
dc30.summary: Add a cart to a coffee-gear store: add from the catalog, a drawer with quantities and totals, and a coupon checked by the API.
dc30.brief:
Ember & Oak sells pour-over gear. App.tsx loads the products (done) and renders ProductCards with an Add to cart button, and a Cart button with a badge stuck at 0.

Read utils/money.ts first: all prices are integer cents, and formatMoney, calcTax (8.25%) and percentOf are there to reuse. In api.ts, validateCoupon(code) takes 0.5–1.0 s and only accepts SAVE10 (any case).

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next. Change (~21 min): free-shipping progress bar.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan · 6–21 Core · 21–26 change · 26–30 Next + talk

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The cart is { productId, qty }[] in App, because the header badge and the drawer both need it. I don't copy names or prices into the cart; the drawer joins with products. Subtotal, discount, tax and total are all derived on every render, in cents, and only formatted at the end. The coupon also lives in App so it survives closing the drawer. The coupon form owns its input, a checking flag and the error message."
requirements: Add to cart adds one of that product (adding again increases its quantity). The header badge shows the total item count

Clicking Cart opens a right-side drawer over a dark backdrop: each line shows the product, − qty + (− disabled at 1), Remove, and the line total. Empty cart: "Your cart is empty." ✕ or the backdrop closes it
Below the lines: Subtotal, Tax (8.25%) and Total, using formatMoney and calcTax. 2 × Ceramic dripper = $56.00, tax $4.62, total $60.62

A coupon field + Apply calls validateCoupon (button reads "Checking…" meanwhile). Invalid: red Code "BOGUS" isn't valid. SAVE10: a green "SAVE10 applied · 10% off" with Remove, and a Discount row. Tax is on the discounted subtotal
The coupon and cart survive closing and reopening the drawer

change.title: Free-shipping progress bar
change.html:
"Marketing wants to nudge order size. Free shipping starts at $75."

  • At the top of the drawer: Add $19.00 more for free shipping with a progress bar (amber fill) showing subtotal / $75.
  • At $75 or more: You've unlocked free shipping, green background, full green bar.
  • Use the subtotal before the discount.
